subject: MSA / Exhibit: inspection carveouts, pen-test notice & evidence cadence
messages:
From: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@havenhealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rpatel@havenhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Exhibit B: audit/pen-test language and evidence cadence

Hi Priya,

Thanks for sending the MSA. HavenHealth legal reviewed Exhibit B (security) and has a few open items we need aligned on before legal clears:

- Audit rights: current draft allows "inspection at any time." We need clearer windows and scope (e.g., sample-based evidence or SOC 2 Type II with redacted artifacts) rather than unlimited disruptive access.
- Pen-testing: need explicit process for notice, approved tester list, and a 30-day notice minimum. Also require coordination with our Ops team for scheduled windows.
- Evidence cadence: SOC 2 Type II report acceptable, but we also ask for quarterly evidence snapshots for scoped controls and 30 days of rolling audit logs for investigation.

I'm attaching our security requirements summary (haven_security_req.pdf). Can we get a short proposed redline for Exhibit B and a recommended cadence from Redwood's side?

Elena
Elena Garcia
Sr. Security Partner | HavenHealth

Elena — thanks, and appreciate the clear asks + the attachment. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Priyom (assurance/ops) to propose concrete redlines and an operational plan.

Proposed next steps:
1) Karthik to send a short legal redline (target today) that balances audit rights with staging/non-disruptive windows.
2) Priyom to propose a pen-test notice process, minimal scheduling SLAs, and recommended evidence cadence (SOC2 + supplemental snapshots).
3) I can coordinate an ops-to-ops call if we need to walk through staging/network constraints.

Can you confirm the HavenHealth preference on: SOC 2 Type II / Type I, and whether the quarterly evidence snapshots must include raw logs or summarized artifacts?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@havenhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA + Exhibit B: audit/pen-test language and evidence cadence

Priya / Elena — I drafted a concise set of redlines for Exhibit B to address the three asks. Main points below (full redline attached in "redline_proposal_security_exhibit.docx"):

1) Audit/Inspection Rights
- Replace open-ended "inspection at any time" language with: "Customer may request evidence and conduct non-disruptive inspections on reasonable notice not to exceed two business windows per 12-month period, except as required to investigate a bona fide security incident."
- Define "reasonable notice" as 10 business days for evidence requests; 30 calendar days for on-site or high-impact inspections.

2) Pen-test / Vulnerability Assessments
- Add a mitigation-first clause: customer must provide 30 calendar days' notice prior to third-party penetration testing.
- Tests must be performed by an agreed vendor (mutual approval) and limited to pre-authorized IP ranges and target scopes; Redwood will provide a readout and remediation ETA within 10 business days of test completion.

3) Evidence cadence & retention
- Accept SOC 2 Type II (most recent report) + quarterly evidence snapshots for scoped controls (architectural diagrams, selected log samples, control testing summaries).
- For raw log access requests, require a security review and a legal NDA/exception; default deliverable is summarized artifacts to protect other customers' telemetry.

Open questions for HavenHealth: is a 10-business-day evidence-request window workable for you? Will quarterly snapshots satisfy your compliance team, or do you need monthly?

Karthik Iyer
Legal Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@havenhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rpatel@havenhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Exhibit B: audit/pen-test language and evidence cadence

Karthik — thanks for the draft language, that helps a lot. A few clarifying items from our side:

- SOC 2 Type II is required; quarterly snapshots should be sufficient if they include control testing summaries and supporting artifacts (we don't need raw streaming logs, but 30 days of rolling logs for investigations is required).
- 10 business days for document/evidence requests is tight but acceptable for summary artifacts; we would still expect a 30-day turnaround for any requests that require deeper forensic artifacts.
- Pen-test notice: 30 calendar days is non-negotiable for us; we prefer a 45-day window for vendor onboarding when third-party testers are not previously approved. Can we compromise to 30 days with a process to expedite to 15 days for urgent red-team assessments (by mutual agreement)?

One additional ask: can Redwood include a short operational runbook (1-pager) that documents the evidence submission format and the contacts for scheduling pen-test windows? That will save time at handoff.

Attachment: haven_security_req.pdf (sent previously)

Elena

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@havenhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, Rajiv Patel <rpatel@havenhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Exhibit B: audit/pen-test language and evidence cadence — agreed next steps

Thanks everyone — summary and proposed execution plan: 

Agreed items:
- SOC 2 Type II accepted as primary evidence; Redwood to provide most recent report and quarterly evidence snapshots (control testing summaries + selected artifacts).
- Audit/inspection: formalize as 2 non-disruptive inspection windows per year; 10 business days notice for summary artifacts, 30 days for deeper requests. Exceptions for bona fide incidents remain.
- Pen-testing: default 30-day notice; 45-day onboarding only if vendor is unvetted. Expedited 15-day option by mutual written agreement. SecureScan Labs may be used pending vendor approval.

Action items (owners & timeline):
- Karthik: finalize redline and send Exhibit B updated doc by EOD tomorrow (owner: legal).
- Priyom: produce a 1-page operational runbook for evidence delivery and pen-test scheduling; aim for two business days.
- Priya: schedule a 30-minute ops sync (HavenOps <> Redwood Ops) this week to walk the runbook and test-window playbook. HubSpot: https://hubspot.example.com/deals/DL-12987

If that all looks right, I'll ask Legal/Procurement at HavenHealth to confirm and we can move to redline exchange + signature.

Best,
